target_customer: Government affairs and lobbying teams at companies, trade groups and nonprofits
problem: Government affairs teams tracked bills, meetings, reports and media mentions across scattered tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for government affairs teams

founders.name: Emil Pitkin
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Founder and CEO and to join Phone2Action leadership after the 2020 deal. Contact-data aggregators in search snippets mention a Harvard degree and a Wharton statistics PhD; not recorded because no opened source states it.

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating legislative, regulatory, lobbying and media data from many public sources into one searchable system took scraping and data cleaning work.

defensibility.rationale: Stored workflows and relationship data could create lock-in, but the public data inputs were available to competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Phone2Action acquired it in November 2020, and its parent Capitol Canary was bought by Quorum in September 2022, which planned to retire the GovPredict platform.

market_need_then: Government affairs teams were an established buyer group with existing paid tracking tools, but no dated 2014 source on spend or complaints was opened.

branding.domain_note: Used govpredict.com, which now redirects to quorum.us.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct tagline 'The system of record for government affairs'

rebrands.why: Quorum acquired parent Capitol Canary and planned to migrate users; the domain now redirects to Quorum

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand itself was found, and the name implies prediction while the product was a government affairs record system.

outcome_analysis: GovPredict built a record system for government affairs teams and reached about 60 people on the YC page. Phone2Action bought it in November 2020 for an undisclosed price, with the CEO joining the acquirer's leadership team, and the platform was later slated to be folded into Quorum after the 2022 deal. Funding was not publicly found, and no source states the reasons for selling, so the story is a mid-sized niche SaaS absorbed during consolidation of public affairs software.
notes: Unverified: Preqin snippet lists a 120K seed led by Y Combinator, aggregator-only, so not recorded as a round. Founders: Marketscreener snippets name Edward Lando and Steve Johnston as co-founders, but neither the YC page nor a company source says so, so they are not listed. CB Insights names Neal Kemp as founder, which conflicts. Technical.ly and CB Insights say launched 2015 while YC says Summer 2014, so the founding year follows the YC page. The Quorum acquisition on LinkedIn is described by a more detailed source as Quorum buying Capitol Canary. No dated competitor source found near 2014, so the list is empty. One search result contained an instruction aimed at AI tools, ignored as data. Completeness pass: Round rests on databases (Seedtable seed 2015-08; CB Insights total 120K), not press. Early Light Ventures is listed by Seedtable but was founded years later, so it is not recorded. The YC page batch (Summer 2014) conflicts with Seedtable's 2015 date.
